claim: Langkawi was recognised as a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2007, the first in Southeast Asia.
quote: Langkawi UNESCO Global Geopark... first geopark in Southeast Asia to receive this designation in 2007.

claim: The geopark comprises Machinchang Cambrian, Kilim Karst and Dayang Bunting Marble geoforest parks plus the Kubang Badak BioGeoTrail, each with distinct geology.
quote: Machinchang Cambrian Geoforest Park (4,274 ha)... Kilim Karst Geoforest Park (4,354 ha)... Dayang Bunting Marble Geoforest Park (8,261 ha)... Kubang Badak BioGeoTrail.

claim: The Sky Bridge is a 125 m curved cable-stayed pedestrian bridge completed in 2005, with its deck at about 660 m above sea level on Gunung Mat Cincang.
quote: a 125-metre (410 ft) curved pedestrian cable-stayed bridge... completed in 2005... deck is 660 metres (2,170 ft) above sea level at the peak of Gunung Mat Cincang.

claim: Panorama Langkawi operates the official SkyCab cable car, SkyBridge, SkyGlide, SkyDome and SkyRex at Oriental Village.
quote: SkyCab... SkyGlide... SkyBridge... SkyDome... SkyRex... Oriental Village, 6D Cinemotion... 3D Art Langkawi... Telaga Tujuh.

claim: International SkyCab 4-in-1 tickets are RM80 adult; standard hours 09:30-18:00, Wednesdays from 12:00, with a full annual closure July 12-24 for maintenance.
quote: 4 in 1 Package (International) Adult: MYR 80.00... Hours: 09:30-18:00... Wednesdays operate from 12:00 PM (maintenance)... Annual Closure: July 12-24.

claim: The SkyBridge is the official curved suspension walkway reached from the cable car top station.
quote: SkyBridge | Official Website for Langkawi Cable Car.

claim: SkyGlide is an inclined lift from the cable car middle station to the SkyBridge costing RM16 adult / RM11 child round trip.
quote: SkyGlide tickets cost RM16 (adults) and RM11 (children) for a round-trip ride to and from SkyBridge.

claim: SkyDome and SkyRex are bundled add-ons many visitors find dated and skippable next to the cable-car ride itself.
quote: Entry Fee covers SkyCab, SkyDome, SkyRex and 3D Art Langkawi.

claim: Cable car combo vouchers carry open-date validity up to 6 months with free cancellation, so no fixed timed slot is required in advance.
quote: voucher has open date validity up to 6 months... Free cancellation and refund is available up to 6 hours before the start time.

claim: The cable car is the single must-do; the southern end of Pantai Cenang down to Pantai Tengah is the best sunset spot.
quote: If you only have time for one thing here, make it Langkawi Cable Car... The southern end, including down to Pantai Tengah, is the best place to catch sunset.

claim: Cable car, Sky Bridge, beaches, Kilim Geoforest and island hopping rank as Langkawi's top attractions.
quote: THE 15 BEST Things to Do in Langkawi (2026) - Must-See Attractions.

claim: Eagle Square (Dataran Lang) is a free public plaza in Kuah centred on a 12 m sea-eagle statue, best at sunrise or sunset over the bay.
quote: Standing at 12-meters high... there is no entrance fee to visit Dataran Lang... best times... early in the morning... or in the evening to catch the beautiful sunset over the bay.

claim: Dataran Lang's eagle references Langkawi's name (helang = eagle) and overlooks Kuah Bay with mountains behind.
quote: Dataran Lang / Eagle Square.

claim: Pantai Cenang is the busy main beach; quieter bays like Tanjung Rhu and Datai Bay offer clearer water and fewer crowds.
quote: Langkawi - Best Beaches with Map.

claim: Tanjung Rhu on the north coast is one of Malaysia's prettiest beaches, backed by casuarina trees and facing limestone islets, with few crowds.
quote: Tanjung Rhu... secluded and peaceful, with stunning views of nearby limestone islands and emerald-green waters.

claim: Pantai Cenang's 2 km strip has the island's main concentration of beachfront bars, restaurants and watersports.
quote: 7 Best Beaches on Langkawi Island.

claim: Telaga Tujuh (Seven Wells) is named for seven rock pools fed by a stream near the cable car / Oriental Village.
quote: Telaga Tujuh Waterfall, or Seven Wells, got its name from the seven small pools.

claim: Reaching the upper Seven Wells pools means climbing 638 steps; entry is about RM10 with RM2 car parking.
quote: A well-maintained staircase of 638 steps leads to the waterfall... The entry fee is 10 ringgit... for a car — 2 ringgit.

claim: Seven Wells is best in the wet/early-dry months when flow is strong; rocks are slippery and monkeys frequent the area.
quote: Telaga Tujuh Waterfalls - All You SHOULD Know Before Going 2026.

claim: Temurun is Langkawi's tallest waterfall, a three-tier drop on the north slope of Mount Mat Cincang in the Datai area, strongest after the wet season.
quote: Temurun is located in Datai Bay area and is a three-tier waterfall... This is the tallest waterfall in Langkawi.

claim: Temurun's first tier is a 5-minute walk from the roadside car park on Jalan Datai; entry is free.
quote: From the car park at the main road, the first tier is only a short distance away (about 5 minutes walk)... Entry is free.

claim: Temurun Waterfall is listed by Langkawi's official tourism body among the island's nature experiences.
quote: Air Terjun Temurun - Visit Langkawi - The Sustainable Paradise Island.

claim: Kilim Geoforest mangrove boat tours run roughly RM65-77 per person shared, or about RM330 for a private boat of up to ten.
quote: Kilim Mangrove private boats cost from RM330 up to 10 people... For shared tours, pricing ranges from RM65 per person... or RM77 per person including a set meal.

claim: Kilim mangrove tours stop at the Bat Cave and Crocodile Cave; better operators now do observation-only eagle watching rather than chicken-skin feeding.
quote: operators practice observation-only eagle watching, not throwing chicken skin into the water... Key stops include the famous Bat Cave and Crocodile Cave.

claim: The classic island-hopping tour visits Dayang Bunting, Singa Besar and Beras Basah islands.
quote: Langkawi Island Hopping Tour Price & Packages.

claim: Island hopping has three stops; Dayang Bunting's freshwater lake is a 10-minute rainforest walk and shared tours start around RM50pp.
quote: three stops that are nicely spaced out. Pulau Dayang Bunting... is a stunning freshwater lake, accessible via a ten-minute walk through the rainforest... sharing tours starting from RM50 per person.

claim: Dayang Bunting (Pregnant Maiden) Island and its Lake of the Pregnant Maiden are a headline island-hopping stop.
quote: Dayang Bunting Island - All You SHOULD Know Before Going (2026 Reviews).

claim: Gunung Raya is Langkawi's highest peak at 881 m, reachable by a winding paved road of about 25 minutes from Kuah with viewpoints en route.
quote: Gunung Raya is the highest peak in Langkawi Island, with a height of 881 meters... From Kuah town, it's about 25 minutes along Jalan Gunung Raya.

claim: Gunung Raya's summit observation tower has been closed/abandoned; views are now from the road and parking area.
quote: the observation tower is closed... a tower with an observation deck is now closed and abandoned.

claim: Pulau Payar Marine Park snorkelling day trips are sold as full-day packages and typically cost under RM400.
quote: Pulau Payar Snorkeling Langkawi | 2026 Book Now Pay Later.

claim: Pulau Payar reviews are split: some praise the clear water and fish, others report dead coral, poor facilities and crowding.
quote: Corals were dead and remain dead. The corals are dead, the toilets/changing rooms are dirty... the place is poorly maintained.

claim: Pulau Payar is considered the best snorkelling option reachable from Langkawi.
quote: Best Langkawi Snorkeling is at Pulau Payar.

claim: The Datai Langkawi is a five-star resort set in ancient rainforest on the island's northwestern tip at Datai Bay.
quote: set on the northwestern tip of the lush tropical island of Langkawi... surrounded by ancient, virgin rainforest.

claim: The Datai's resident naturalists run guided nature walks including the Rimba Trail, canopy walkway, birdwatching and mangrove kayaking.
quote: Rimba Trail... begins in a littoral or coastal forest before transitioning into a mangrove swamp over a 70 m-elevated walkway... birdwatching walks... canopy walkway.

claim: Datai Bay's beach has been named among National Geographic's Top 10 beaches worldwide.
quote: Datai Bay's idyllic white-sand beach, one of the Top 10 Beaches worldwide as awarded by National Geographic.

claim: Telaga Harbour at Pantai Kok is one of only two Langkawi marinas where yachts can clear in and out, with a waterfront dining quay.
quote: Telaga Harbour - Langkawi Gateway Marina.

claim: Telaga Harbour Park's Perdana Quay boardwalk has waterfront restaurants and is a scenic sunset spot near Pantai Kok.
quote: Telaga Harbour is home to Perdana Quay, a modern shopping complex... boardwalk and waterside restaurants... Visit during sunset for breathtaking views.

claim: Pantai Cenang/Tengah and Tanjung Rhu are among the best places to watch sunset in Langkawi.
quote: Best Places to Watch the Sunset in Langkawi.

claim: Underwater World Langkawi draws criticism as run-down with cramped, distressing enclosures; widely advised to skip.
quote: the facility feels 'extremely run down' and 'quite distressing'... animals appear unhealthy and are kept in enclosures that are far too small.

claim: Crocodile Adventureland is critiqued as feeling like a zoo lacking adventure, of limited appeal beyond curiosity.
quote: sadly lacking in adventure... basically feels like a zoo. Just for crocodiles.

claim: Crocodile Adventureland houses over 4,000 crocodiles and runs feeding shows.
quote: The Largest Crocodile Adventureland in Malaysia | Crocodile Shows | Crocodile Feeding.

claim: The Kubang Badak BioGeoTrail offers mangroves, ancient sea caves, 500-million-year-old fossils and Thai-Malay heritage on a guided eco-tour.
quote: mangroves, ancient caves, fossil sites, and Thai-Malay heritage on a guided eco-tour... 500-million-year-old trilobite fossils.

claim: Kubang Badak BioGeoTrail is promoted by Malaysia's national tourism body as a geopark highlight.
quote: Celebrating World Tourism Day: The Wonders Of Kubang Badak Biogeotrail.

claim: Offbeat Langkawi experiences include quiet caves, mangroves and lesser-visited beaches away from Cenang.
quote: Langkawi Hidden Gems: 10 Offbeat Experiences You Must Try.

claim: Langkawi's caves include Gua Cerita (Cave of Legends) and bat caves reached only by boat in the Kilim/Tanjung Rhu area.
quote: Langkawi Caves - Gua Cerita, Gua Kelawar, Gua Langsiar, Gua Buaya.

claim: Langkawi's dry season runs roughly November to March/April with the southwest monsoon and heaviest rain May to October.
quote: In May, the Southwest Monsoon starts to blow, bringing plenty of rain; in November, Langkawi enters its dry season.

claim: November-March offers the driest weather and clearest seas but 30%+ higher hotel prices; September-October is the wettest stretch.
quote: best time to visit Langkawi is during its dry season... hotel prices go up 30% higher... the worst of the Langkawi monsoon season which occurs in during September and October.

claim: In June 2026 1 MYR was about 0.217 EUR, i.e. roughly 1 EUR to 4.6 MYR.
quote: As of June 2, 2026, 1 Malaysian Ringgit equals 0.2169 Euros.

claim: The Sky Bridge closes in bad weather, so cable-car visits can be disrupted with little notice.
quote: Langkawi Sky Bridge - All You SHOULD Know Before Going (2026 Reviews).
